title: 388. The Fall of the Aztecs: The Festival of Blood (Part 5)

sentences.en: In the Temple Square, the drummers struck up a pounding rhythm.
sentences.zh: 在圣殿广场上，鼓手们敲响了沉重的节奏。

sentences.en: The dancers joined hands once again.
sentences.zh: 舞者们再次手牵着手。

sentences.en: Four hundred of the bravest and strongest young men in the city.
sentences.zh: 那是城里四百名最勇敢、最强壮的年轻人。

sentences.en: The crowds began to chant and clap.
sentences.zh: 人群开始吟唱并拍手。

sentences.en: Hundreds and hundreds of men, women and children, their faces shining with religious excitement.
sentences.zh: 成百上千的男女老少，脸上洋溢着宗教般的狂热。

sentences.en: None of them, of course, had brought weapons.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们谁也没有携带武器。

sentences.en: Round and round, the dancers whirled faster and faster.
sentences.zh: 舞者们转啊转，越转越快。

sentences.en: The drummers hammered louder and louder.
sentences.zh: 鼓声敲得越来越响。

sentences.en: The sun beat down hotter and hotter.
sentences.zh: 太阳晒得越来越烫。

sentences.en: In their excitement, nobody noticed the Spaniards closing the gates leading out of the Temple Precinct and taking up their positions around the edge of the square.
sentences.zh: 在兴奋之中，没人注意到西班牙人正关上通往圣殿区域的大门，并在广场边缘各就各位。

sentences.en: Round and round went the dancers in wave after wave of joy and passion, louder and louder, hotter and hotter, faster and faster.
sentences.zh: 舞者们一波又一波地旋转着，充满喜悦与激情，声音越来越大，天气越来越热，速度越来越快。

sentences.en: Alvarado drew his sword.

sentences.zh: 他的双眼在燃烧。

sentences.zh: 这根本不是他们当初加入时所预想的。

sentences.en: The worst holiday ever.
sentences.zh: 史上最糟糕的假期。

sentences.en: There must be some Tlashkarlans and maybe Tottenacks, we don't know, lurking around as well.
sentences.zh: 肯定还有一些特拉斯卡拉人，也许还有托托纳克人，我们不知道，也在附近潜伏着。

sentences.en: How many of them?
sentences.zh: 他们有多少人？

sentences.en: It's impossible to say.
sentences.zh: 无法估计。

sentences.en: Among the Spaniards, you can imagine them kind of there, camped in corridors and chambers and bedrooms and whatever of this palace, crammed in, sweaty, bloodstained, hungry, wet.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象一下西班牙人的处境，他们挤在这座宫殿的走廊、房间和卧室里，拥挤不堪，汗流浃背，满身血迹，饥肠辘辘，浑身湿透。

sentences.en: It's a classic science fiction thing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这很像经典的科幻桥段，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You're stuck in the spaceship.
sentences.zh: 你被困在宇宙飞船里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You've run out of ammunition.
sentences.zh: 你的弹药耗尽了。

sentences.en: It's the plot of aliens or something.
sentences.zh: 这就是《异形》之类的电影情节。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The aliens are outside and they're all waiting to come and lay their eggs in your stomach.
sentences.zh: 外星人在外面，等着进来在你的肚子里产卵。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, Bernal Diaz says, we were to be sacrificed to their gods.
sentences.zh: 我是说，贝尔纳尔·迪亚斯说，我们注定要被献祭给他们的神灵。

sentences.en: Our hearts were to be torn from our bodies.
sentences.zh: 我们的心脏要被从身体里掏出来。

sentences.en: The blood was to be drawn from our veins and our arms and legs were to be eaten at their festivals.
sentences.zh: 血液要从我们的静脉中流干，我们的手臂和腿要在他们的节日里被吃掉。

sentences.en: Our other body parts would be thrown to the tigers, lions and serpents, which hadn't been fed for days.
sentences.zh: 我们身体的其他部位会被扔给老虎、狮子和蛇，它们已经好几天没喂食了。

sentences.en: So they would devour our flesh with real enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 所以它们会非常热切地吞噬我们的血肉。

sentences.en: I mean, this is obviously pure projection.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这显然纯粹是心理投射。

sentences.en: He doesn't know any of this.
sentences.zh: 他根本不知道这些。

sentences.en: Well, there are no tigers and lions, are there?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里根本没有老虎和狮子，对吧？

sentences.en: You already pointed this out.
sentences.zh: 你之前已经指出了这一点。

sentences.en: But this is probably exactly what they're thinking.
sentences.zh: 但这很可能正是他们所想的。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: That nothing good is coming.
sentences.zh: 觉得没什么好下场。

sentences.en: There are stories that they start seeing omens, headless men.
sentences.zh: 有传言说他们开始看到预兆，比如无头人。

sentences.en: One man says he'd seen a head walking around outside attached only to a foot.
sentences.zh: 有人说他看到一个头在外面走动，下面只连着一只脚。

sentences.en: Imagine that with kind of hopping.
sentences.zh: 想象一下那种蹦蹦跳跳的样子。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是啊，没错。

sentences.en: That probably didn't happen to him, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想那大概不是真的发生在他身上。

sentences.en: That's the kind of thing you take if you go into the depths of Mexico and take certain substances.
sentences.zh: 如果你深入墨西哥腹地并服用某些物质，就会看到那种东西。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's what you'd see.
sentences.zh: 你看到的就会是那样。

sentences.en: At some point, obviously, Cortez decides, okay, we're in desperation now.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，显然科尔特斯决定，好吧，我们现在走投无路了。

sentences.en: We'll bring Montezuma out.
sentences.zh: 我们把蒙特祖马带出来。

sentences.en: We'll give it one more go.
sentences.zh: 我们再试一次。

sentences.en: And they take him out onto the roof again.
sentences.zh: 于是他们再次把他带到屋顶上。

sentences.en: And this is this very, very, very famous scene.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个非常、非常、非常著名的场景。

sentences.en: There are people throwing stones, firing arrows, all this, whenever they see a Spaniard.
sentences.zh: 人们一看到西班牙人，就会扔石头、射箭，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So as soon as Cortez goes out onto the roof, this hail of missiles, some of the Spaniards use their shields to protect Montezuma.
sentences.zh: 所以当科尔特斯一走到屋顶上，就遭到了箭雨般的攻击，一些西班牙人用盾牌保护蒙特祖马。

sentences.en: And they bring him out.
sentences.zh: 他们把他带了出来。

sentences.en: And when the crowd sees the emperor, they stop.
sentences.zh: 当人群看到皇帝时，他们停了下来。

sentences.en: And there's this sort of hush.
sentences.zh: 出现了一种寂静。

sentences.en: And Montezuma, God knows how.
sentences.zh: 而蒙特祖马，天知道他是怎么做到的。

sentences.en: Is he imposing?
sentences.zh: 他威严吗？

sentences.en: Is he exhausted and terrified?
sentences.zh: 他精疲力竭且惊恐万分吗？

sentences.en: Is he in despair?
sentences.zh: 他绝望吗？

sentences.en: Is he begging?
sentences.zh: 他在乞求吗？

sentences.en: But he says to them, you know, hear me, people of the Mexica or something like that.
sentences.zh: 但他对他们说，你们知道，听我说，墨西哥的人民，或者类似的话。

sentences.en: And then, as if it's a signal, though probably it wasn't a signal, but as if it's a signal, the crowd start throwing more stuff at him.
sentences.zh: 然后，就像是一个信号，虽然可能并不是信号，但就像是一个信号，人群开始向他投掷更多的东西。

sentences.en: They just drown him out with jeers.
sentences.zh: 他们用嘲笑声淹没了他。

sentences.en: And as one Spaniard says, it was as if the heavens were raining, stones, arrows, darts, and bricks.
sentences.zh: 正如一位西班牙人所说，那就像天上下起了雨，石头、箭、飞镖和砖块。

sentences.en: And Montezuma is hit by a stone.
sentences.zh: 蒙特祖马被一块石头击中了。

sentences.en: Or is he?
sentences.zh: 还是说他没有？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's plausible that he could be hit.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为他被击中是合理的。

sentences.en: The Spaniards claim he's hit.
sentences.zh: 西班牙人声称他被击中了。

sentences.en: This feels like it could happen.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是可能发生的事。

sentences.en: It could easily happen.
sentences.zh: 这很容易发生。

sentences.en: That the people down below are hotheads.
sentences.zh: 下面的人都是些冲动之徒。

sentences.en: There may well be people in the crowd saying, he's sold us out to the strangers from the sea.
sentences.zh: 人群中很可能有人在说，他把我们出卖给了来自海上的陌生人。

sentences.en: So Matthew Ressler, in his book, suggests there are five theories as to how he might have died.
sentences.zh: 所以马修·雷斯勒在他的书中提出了关于他可能如何死亡的五种理论。

sentences.en: So projectiles and it's manslaughter.
sentences.zh: 所以是投掷物导致的过失杀人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Or that the people down there are deliberately trying to kill Montezuma.
sentences.zh: 或者是下面的人蓄意要杀死蒙特祖马。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In which case it's murder.
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，那就是谋杀。

sentences.en: That Montezuma kind of kills himself.
sentences.zh: 蒙特祖马某种程度上是自杀。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: That he's deliberately exposing himself because he's in despair.
sentences.zh: 他因为绝望而故意让自己暴露在危险中。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: The fourth one is that Cuauhtemoc, who we haven't mentioned yet.
sentences.zh: 第四种是库奥特莫克，我们还没提到他。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Who is kind of the hot-headed relative who is keen to succeed him.
sentences.zh: 他是个急躁的亲戚，一心想继承王位。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That he's responsible.
sentences.zh: 是他干的。

sentences.en: And then the fifth is that the Spaniards kill him.
sentences.zh: 第五种是西班牙人杀了他。

sentences.en: Well.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That they're stabbed to death.
sentences.zh: 他们被刺死了。

sentences.en: So there's an odd detail in one of the accounts written by a Jesuit.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一份由耶稣会士撰写的记录中有一个奇怪的细节。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Who says that there were those who said that in order for the wound, i.e. the stab, not to be seen, they put a sword into his nether regions.
sentences.zh: 有人说，为了不让人看到伤口，也就是刺伤，他们把一把剑插进了他的下体。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In other words, the Spanish stab him up his ass.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，西班牙人把剑捅进了他的屁股。

sentences.en: It's so Tom Holland to go for the nether regions story.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰（Tom Holland）居然会去讲下体这种故事，真有他的。

sentences.en: And there's another weird story that his body gets kind of lifted up.
sentences.zh: 还有另一个奇怪的说法，说他的身体被抬了起来。

sentences.en: His sword's been run up through his ass and they're kind of lifting him up on the sword and waving him around on the roof, which seems very improbable.
sentences.zh: 说他的剑从屁股捅进去，他们就把他用剑挑起来，在屋顶上挥舞，这看起来非常不可信。

sentences.en: I think that's very improbable.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常不可信。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I'll give you my accounts in just a second, but here is the absolute standard accounts from Bernal Diaz.
sentences.zh: 所以我待会儿会给出我的看法，但这里先引用贝尔纳·迪亚斯（Bernal Diaz）最标准的记述。

sentences.en: Bernal Diaz says he was hit by these missiles on the roof.
sentences.zh: 贝尔纳·迪亚斯说，他在屋顶上被这些投射物击中了。

sentences.en: The Spaniards took him downstairs.
sentences.zh: 西班牙人把他带到了楼下。

sentences.en: They bandaged his wounds and they asked him to take something that would strengthen him, but he refused as though he'd lost the will to live.
sentences.zh: 他们为他包扎伤口，并让他吃点东西补充体力，但他拒绝了，就好像已经失去了求生的意志。

sentences.en: Bernal Diaz says, contrary to all expectation, we soon heard that he had expired.
sentences.zh: 贝尔纳·迪亚斯说，出乎所有人的意料，我们很快就听说他已经去世了。

sentences.en: Cortez, his officers, and all of us shed tears for this unfortunate monarch.
sentences.zh: 科尔特斯、他的军官们，还有我们所有人都为这位不幸的君主落泪。

sentences.en: Indeed, many of our men who had been in constant attendance upon him mourned for him as if they'd lost a parent.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们许多一直侍奉他的人，哀悼他就像失去了自己的亲人一样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So throughout this series and just recently, you've been comparing Cortez and the Spaniards to Caesar and his legions.
sentences.zh: 所以在这整个系列节目中，包括最近，你一直把科尔特斯和西班牙人比作凯撒和他的军团。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the scene of Caesar weeping over the death of Pompey.
sentences.zh: 还有凯撒为庞培之死而哭泣的那一幕。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: His rival and his friend.
sentences.zh: 他的对手，也是他的朋友。

sentences.en: This is the kind of the language that you would expect from a classically educated historian who is trying to elevate the stature of Cortez, which I guess Diaz is definitely doing.
sentences.zh: 这正是那种受过古典教育的历史学家会用的语言，他们试图提升科尔特斯的地位，我想迪亚斯绝对是在这么做。

sentences.en: Is clearly doing.
sentences.zh: 显然是在这么做。

sentences.en: I think it's utterly, utterly implausible, that story.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那个故事完全、完全不可信。

sentences.en: I suppose it's plausible that Montezuma would have lost the will to live to some extent.
sentences.zh: 我想蒙特祖玛在某种程度上失去求生意志倒是可能的。

sentences.en: That is plausible.
sentences.zh: 那是有可能的。

sentences.en: But the spectacle of Cortez, this man who has proved himself so cold-blooded, ruthless and opportunistic,
sentences.zh: 但科尔特斯这个被证明如此冷血、无情且投机的人，

sentences.en: standing there with tears rolling down his cheeks at the death of his great friend.
sentences.zh: 站在那里，看着他伟大的朋友死去，泪流满面，这景象……

sentences.en: I mean, against that, the Spanish have killed a lot of kings before.
sentences.zh: 我是说，反过来看，西班牙人以前杀过很多国王。

sentences.en: I mean, then queens.
sentences.zh: 我是说，还有王后。

sentences.en: They killed Queen on Hispaniola.
sentences.zh: 他们在伊斯帕尼奥拉岛杀过王后。

sentences.en: Yeah, they did.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们杀过。

sentences.en: Killed Hachui in Cuba.
sentences.zh: 在古巴杀过哈丘伊（Hachui）。

sentences.en: I mean, they're not exactly reticent about it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对此并不避讳。

sentences.en: But don't forget, it's important to them to claim that he had surrendered to them.
sentences.zh: 但别忘了，对他们来说，声称他已经投降是很重要的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He can't be their enemy.
sentences.zh: 他不能是他们的敌人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that's the explanation, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这就是解释，不是吗？

sentences.en: I think.
sentences.zh: 我想是吧。

sentences.en: Now, there is a hint in an indigenous source of a very different version.
sentences.zh: 现在，在一个本土文献中有一个暗示，提到了一个非常不同的版本。

sentences.en: This is a book called The History of the Indies of New Spain, which was published in 1581 by a guy called Diego Duran, who was a Dominican.
sentences.zh: 这是一本名为《新西班牙印度群岛史》的书，由一位名叫迭戈·杜兰（Diego Duran）的多米尼加修士于1581年出版。

sentences.en: He is not obviously indigenous, but he based it on Nahuatl sources.
sentences.zh: 他显然不是土著，但他基于纳瓦特尔语的资料编写了这本书。

sentences.en: So it's not just indigenous.
sentences.zh: 所以它不仅仅是本土的。

sentences.en: It has a hint of Spanish in it as well.
sentences.zh: 里面也带有一点西班牙人的色彩。

sentences.en: He says that after the Spanish had left Tenochtitlan, which we'll come to tomorrow, the Mexica burst into the building.
sentences.zh: 他说，在西班牙人离开特诺奇蒂特兰之后——我们明天会讲到——墨西加人冲进了大楼。

sentences.en: They found Montezuma with a chain about his feet and five dagger wounds in his cheSt.
sentences.zh: 他们发现蒙特祖玛脚上戴着锁链，胸口有五处刀伤。

sentences.en: Nearby lay the nobles and great lords that had been held prisoner with him.
sentences.zh: 附近躺着和他一起被囚禁的贵族和显贵们。

sentences.en: And you mentioned the Jesuit source that say that the Spaniards shoved the sword in his nether regions.
sentences.zh: 你提到了那个耶稣会士的资料，说西班牙人把剑捅进了他的下体。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think the nether regions thing to me smacks too much of what happens to kings.
sentences.zh: 我觉得下体那个说法，太像那种针对国王的典型套路了。

sentences.en: You know, Edward II.
sentences.zh: 你知道，爱德华二世那种。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: All these kinds of things, that it's too much of a standard device.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情，这太像是一种标准化的叙事手段了。

sentences.en: But is it plausible that they would have had him chained and that they would have stabbed him in the chest?
sentences.zh: 但他们把他锁起来并刺穿他的胸膛，这合理吗？

sentences.en: I think absolutely it is because he clearly is no longer useful to them.
sentences.zh: 我觉得绝对合理，因为他显然对他们来说已经没有利用价值了。

sentences.en: If his own people won't listen to him, what is the point?
sentences.zh: 如果他自己的人民都不听他的，那还有什么意义？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What's the value?
sentences.zh: 有什么价值？

sentences.en: What is the point of keeping him alive?
sentences.zh: 留着他活命还有什么意义？

sentences.en: He's just a focus for rebellion and resistance because we know they killed other people, his advisors and other nobles.
sentences.zh: 他只是叛乱和抵抗的焦点，因为我们知道他们杀死了其他人，包括他的顾问和其他贵族。

sentences.en: It's also a very brutally decisive statement of the resolution that Cortez presumably by this point has taken, which is they have no choice but to get out.
sentences.zh: 这同时也是一个非常残酷且果断的声明，表明科尔特斯此时此刻大概已经下定决心，那就是他们别无选择，只能撤退。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, negotiations are not going to work.
sentences.zh: 你知道，谈判是行不通的。

sentences.en: And in a way, it's kind of, again, a crossing of the Rubicon.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这又是一种“跨越卢比孔河”的行为。

sentences.en: If you kill your hostage, then that leaves you with no option but to try and make your escape.
sentences.zh: 如果你杀了你的人质，那就意味着你别无选择，只能尝试逃跑。

sentences.en: And that, Dominic, is the story for tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 而那，多米尼克，就是明天的故事了。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: So I think exactly that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以我完全同意，汤姆。

sentences.en: I think they've killed Montezuma because they don't want to take him with them because at this point, they have decided somehow, Tom, they have to get out of this city.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们杀了蒙特祖玛，是因为他们不想带他一起走，因为此时此刻，汤姆，他们不知何故已经决定必须逃离这座城市。

sentences.en: And the story of how they do it is the most extraordinary kind of, it's like something from an action movie times 100.
sentences.zh: 而他们逃跑的故事简直太不可思议了，就像动作电影情节放大了100倍一样。

sentences.en: The Noce Triste, it's called, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 叫“悲伤之夜”（Noce Triste），对吧？

sentences.en: The Sad Night.
sentences.zh: 悲伤之夜。

sentences.en: Yeah, we'll come to that tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们明天会讲到。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that will be tomorrow's episode.
sentences.zh: 所以那将是明天的节目内容。

sentences.en: But if you just can't wait, you know the form.
sentences.zh: 但如果你等不及了，你知道规矩的。

sentences.en: I've been repeating this at the end of every episode, but I'm contractually obliged to do this because if I don't, Theo will shout at me.
sentences.zh: 我在每一集结尾都在重复这个，但我有合同义务必须这么做，因为如果我不做，西奥（Theo）会对我大吼大叫。

sentences.en: So you can find out if the Spaniards make their escape, if they do, how they do it by signing up to the Restless History Club and you will get access to it straight away.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以通过注册“不安历史俱乐部”（Restless History Club）来了解西班牙人是否成功逃脱，如果成功了，他们是怎么做到的，你可以立即获得访问权限。

sentences.en: But if you want to wait, then do by all means wait.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想等，那就尽管等吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, what you've done there, which is very nice, is you've cast yourself as Montezuma, Theo as Hernan Cortez, and that makes me Pedro de Alvarado.
sentences.zh: 是的，你刚才做得很好，你把自己设定为蒙特祖玛，西奥是埃尔南·科尔特斯，那我就成了佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多（Pedro de Alvarado）。

sentences.en: So I'm going to be keeping my legs crossed before we get on to the next episode.
sentences.zh: 所以在进入下一集之前，我得把腿夹紧了。

sentences.en: Very nice.
sentences.zh: 非常好。

sentences.en: So we'll see you either in a few minutes or tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 那么我们几分钟后见，或者明天见。

sentences.en: Hasta luego.
sentences.zh: 回头见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
